Prince Harry says he wants to reconcile with King Charles, Prince William and the rest of his family after a six-year rift over his move to the US and criticism of royal life. He said, “the most important thing is to reconcile” and urged everyone to “let go of the past”, adding that “there’s enough drama in the world” to keep family conflict going. Harry also said returning to Britain has helped his children enjoy a British school, and he hopes his tense relationship with the British press can improve, Reuters reported.

LONDON - Prince Harry has said he hoped to reconcile with King Charles and the rest of his family with whom he fell out when he moved to the United States six years ago. Harry, 42, the king’s younger son, caused a huge rupture in the British royal family when he and his wife Meghan quit royal duties and moved to California in 2020 from where they were highly critical of the institution. He has barely spoken to his older brother, heir Prince William, for years, and his family has only recently met up again with his father.

In an interview with GQ magazine, Harry, who recently relocated back to Britain with Meghan and their two children, said he wanted to patch things up. ‘Most important thing is to reconcile’ “With everything else that’s going on in the world, the most important thing is to reconcile,” he told GQ. He said he could understand the fascination with his family’s situation as people could relate to it.

“There’s sibling disagreements, there’s broken relationships between kids and their parents, kids and one parent,” he said. Some people might be inspired by efforts to reconcile and this could help their own relationships. “And some people don’t want it to work out. I want it to work out,” he added.

Harry’s spokesperson said those latter comments were not meant as a swipe at William or any other family members. Harry, the Duke of Sussex, went on to tell GQ that while “scars stick around forever”, he wanted to encourage everybody to let go of the past. “For me, there’s enough drama in the world and enough drama in people’s lives than to continue with issues with family,” he said. “It’s not worth it.” Children ‘loving’ UK school In the lengthy interview, Harry also discussed themes he has previously talked about, such as the impact of losing his mother Princess Diana when he was 12 and his mental health struggles. But he also talked about why he had returned to Britain, saying that being able to put his children in a British school “has meant a lot to me”. “I didn’t know how important it was to me. I always thought it was going to be something that we would try and do, but now they’ve been in school for two weeks. They’re loving it, and it’s just giving them a whole different experience.” He also said he hoped that his fraught relationship with the British press, which partly led to him leaving in the first place and has led to a number of lawsuits against newspaper groups, would now be better. “My hope is that it will change,” he said. “There have been some battles that have been fought, necessarily so. But hopefully, we can all draw a line under that. “As with everything else that’s going on in the world, there are aspects of the past that I’m sure all of us, me, my family, some of the British press, that we’d all like to leave behind us and work for the greater good.” REUTERS
